summary: Monthly company all-hands. Avery opened with company performance highlights (ARR growth, runway, hiring pace). Samir gave a tech update: runtime optimizations, private deployment milestones, and a benchmark ask for Dedicated customers. Maya shared product roadmap for December including Redwood Optimize features and a focus on quality/regression tooling. Nina summarized go-to-market progress: top line, key renewals, and new Dedicated commitments. People Ops gave a brief hiring update and comp/benefits reminders. transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good morning, good afternoon, wherever you are. We'll kick off in about a minute, thanks for being on time. Um, quick housekeeping: recording is on, slides are pinned.
[00:18] Avery Chen: Alright let's go. High level - great month for the company. ARR is up double digits quarter over quarter, we're seeing strong traction in mid-market and a few nice Dedicated commitments that will help with predictability. Not gonna get into numbers on this call but finance will share the update after.
[00:40] Samir Patel: Quick tech update from infra. We shipped the new continuous-batching optimization last week, it's live in hosted and we've already seen a 12% token cost reduction on average for async workloads, and latency is stable. There's one caveat with very short prompt workloads where batching adds tail latency, so we're shipping a micro-config to disable batching for sub-50ms targets.
[01:05] Maya Ortiz: On product - December roadmap highlights: Redwood Optimize beta expansion, improved quantization profiles, and a prompt-eval integration that ties regression alerts to eval sets. We're also prioritizing tooling around rollouts - canary/A-B and automatic fallback when a model variant underperforms.
[01:27] Jordan Li: On Private / VPC deployments - ops team completed the on-prem install test with ACME Health last week, their network team flagged a KMS integration nuance, turned out to be an HSM key wrapping policy. We've fixed the installer script and updated docs. We'll run a dedicated benchmark suite next week to validate throughput on customer's air-gapped setup.
[01:50] Nina Rao: GTM update - pipeline healthy, renewals are trending positive, we closed 3 new mid-market logos this month and have 2 pipeline deals that could convert to Dedicated in Q1. Important ask: sales folks please log Dedicated interest in the new deal-stage field in CRM so we can forecast capacity needs.
[02:14] Audience question (Raj, Eng): Hey Samir, can you say more about the KV cache improvements?
[02:20] Samir Patel: Yeah - so the KV cache evictions were causing unnecessary recomputation for some session patterns. We tuned the eviction policy, reduced cold-starts on repeated sessions. The transcripting here might say 'K V cash' - sorry for the spelling. The net result is better sustained throughput for multi-turn chat.
[02:45] Avery Chen: Quick finance note - runway is in a good spot, we continue to be disciplined on spend. We want to invest in the product and hiring where it matters most: infra, research, and GTM.
[03:02] Maya Ortiz: On Optimize - the tooling will recommend batching and quantization settings per workload, but engineers can override; we want to avoid black box decisions, so we'll include explanation logs in the console.
[03:22] Ethan Brooks: Research update - we validated a new 4-bit quantization pass that preserves quality on roughly 70% of our test evals; for some instruction-following tasks we see small regressions so we'll gate that behind per-model quality checks.
[03:40] Priya Singh: CS update: onboarding health is improving, time-to-first-success (TTFS) down 18% since May. We're continuing to build onboarding templates for Dedicated and Private. Also SOC 2 - we've engaged an auditor; plan is to do readiness prep in December and audit in January.
[04:02] People Ops (voice): Hiring update - we're at 150 headcount, hiring for infra, applied research, and sales. Reminder: internal referral window opens this week, details in the #people channel. Also holiday PTO guidance coming next week.
[04:20] Avery Chen: Alright let's go into a quick demo/preview from Maya on the product dashboard. Slides: "Console - per-route latency & cost" (shared).
[04:32] Maya Ortiz: Screenshot here shows token-level breakdown, you can see per-route cost, tracing hooks, and ability to pin model versions. The new change is a quality regression panel linking eval prompts to live traffic. If a regression is detected it raises an alert and suggests rollback to previous pinned version.
[04:58] Audience comment (Lena, Sales): That's huge for our enterprise accounts, they really want that tie between evals and production.
[05:05] Nina Rao: Yep, we'll use that in renewal conversations - it answers the "how do we detect regressions" question directly.
[05:12] Q (Engineering): Any timeline for making the rollback automatic?
[05:16] Maya Ortiz: We plan to support automatic fallback for 1st wave clients by late January, but default will be manual with canary options.
[05:26] [07:00] Avery Chen: Okay, before we go into Q&A live - a few wins to call out: great work on the Dedicated onboarding guide, special kudos to Jordan and the docs team. Also shout-out to research for the quantization pass.
[07:20] Jordan Li: Thanks - team did a lot of testing. On benchmarking: we're standardizing the benchmark harness, expect an internal doc and spreadsheet. Engineers, please ping infra-bench for access if you need to run custom suites.
[07:40] Q (All): SOC 2 - what's the timeline and who is involved?
[07:45] Priya Singh: Auditor engaged, readiness prep in December, audit window in January. CS and Eng security leads will run a series of evidence collection tasks; we'll post a timeline in Confluence. Action: Priya to run workshop with Eng on 11/24.
[08:03] Audience side conversation (murmur)
[08:10] Avery Chen: Ok - product roadmap callouts - December will be a heavy month for Optimize and rollout tooling, but also small improvements to latency SLOs. Important note: we will start a canary with a small subset of high-value customers to validate automatic fallbacks.
[08:30] Samir Patel: Also infrastructure note - we are evaluating node types for Dedicated to reduce unit cost. There's tradeoff work to do between throughput per GPU vs. chip-level latency. We'll present options to execs next week.
[09:00] Nina Rao: From GTM, please flag any customers asking for private deployment - we have a backlog and we need to queue them against Dedicated capacity.
[09:12] Avery Chen: People Ops - quick note on compensation and retention: we want to be competitive; we'll share updated bands and promotion cadence by end of month.
[09:25] People Ops voice: Yup - expect a doc in the handbook and a Q&A session.
[09:35] [15:00] Q (SC, Sales): Any update on OpenAI or Anthropic integrations or competitive responses?
[15:12] Nina Rao: We talk to customers about model stewardship vs raw access. For most of our customers, predictable performance, observability, and on-prem options are more important than a single newest model. That said we do monitor their feature launches.
[15:35] Samir Patel: On integrations - we support multiple model backends, and our runtime can route to different variants. There's occasional mis-transcription in this note where "route" may be spelled 'root' - anyway.
[16:05] Avery Chen: Alright let's do a lightning round of team shoutouts - five minutes.
[21:00] Shoutouts and applause noises (emoji reactions)
[23:30] [30:00] Live Q&A: 
Q: Are we open to co-selling with cloud partners for Private?
A (Nina): Yes, we're exploring marketplace listings and channel partnerships in EMEA and APAC for Private deployments.
Q: Any blockers on on-prem installs?
A (Jordan): The main blockers are networking and KMS policies; the installer improvements should smooth that out. We'll keep a short checklist for CSMs.
[33:10] [40:00] Deep question from Eng (Tara): For the new 4-bit quant pass, how are we validating safety and hallucination rates?
[40:10] Ethan Brooks: We're running eval suites across multiple instruction-following datasets; where we see increased hallucination we're dropping the quant profile or increasing precision. We'll tie regression alerts to those evals.
[41:00] [47:00] Avery Chen: Final thoughts - we are in a position to double down on product-market fit areas: mid-market, Dedicated, and security-conscious enterprises. Please keep defect rates low and focus on end-to-end customer success for new Dedicated deals.
[47:30] Maya Ortiz: Reminder: roadmap doc and feature demos will be posted next week, watch the product channel.
[48:00] Priya Singh: Reminder about SOC 2 prep and the 11/24 workshop.
[48:12] Nina Rao: Sales please log Dedicated interest in CRM, use the new field.
[48:20] Avery Chen: Ok that's it - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with slide deck and recording.
[48:35] Closing remarks and applause.
